semin-durr:1-1.t:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
The majority read «يَسِيْنْ» with sukūn on the nūn. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, Ḥafṣ, Qālūn and Warsh (with a divergence reported from him) pronounced the nūn clearly before the wāw that follows it, and likewise the nūn of {ن والقلم} [al-Qalam: 1]; the rest assimilated (idghām) both. Whoever assimilated did so for lightness, and because, when the two run on and two close-sounding letters meet from two words, the first with sukūn, assimilation becomes obligatory. Whoever pronounced clearly did so to exaggerate the separation of these letters from one another, because it is with the intention of pausing; this is more in line with analogy for the disjoined letters, and for that reason two sukūns meet in them in continuous recitation, and, in one opinion, the vowel of the hamzat al-waṣl is transferred to them, as in {ألف لام ميم الله}, as its establishment has already been given.
The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr inclined (imāla) the yāʾ of «يس», because it is one of the names, as its establishment was given at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Baqara. Al-Fārisī said: "If they incline «يا», which is a particle of vocative, then they are the more fitting to incline the «يا» of «يس»."
ʿĪsā and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with fatḥa on the nūn: either as indeclinability on the fatḥa for lightness, like أَيْن and كيفَ; or as an object of «اتْلُ» ("recite"); or as genitive by the particle of oath. On both aspects it is a diptote (ghayr munṣarif), by reason of being a proper name and feminine. It may also be accusative by removal of the particle of oath, as in his saying:
3774 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فذاك أمانةَ اللَّهِ الثَّريدُ
(... that, by the trust of Allah, is the tharīd.)
Al-Kalbī read it with ḍamma on the nūn. It was said: [this is] because it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is يس", and it was prevented from tanwīn for the reason given. And it was said: rather it is a vowel of indeclinability like حيث; so it may be a khabar as stated, or something sworn by, like "ʿahd Allāhi, I shall surely do it". And it was said: because it is a vocative and so was made indeclinable on the ḍamma; for this reason al-Kalbī, who recited it so, explained it as «يا إنسانُ» ("O human"), and said: "It is the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If its meaning is sound, then its explanation is that its origin is يا أُنَيْسِيْنُ, and the vocative with it became so frequent on their tongues that they confined themselves to half of it, as they said in the oath: مُ الله for ايْمُنُ اللَّهِ." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What is reported from the Arabs for the diminutive of إنْسان is أُنَيْسِيان, with a yāʾ followed by an alif, which indicates that its origin is إنْسِيان, because the diminutive returns things to their origins, and we do not know that they said أُنَيْسِين in its diminutive. And supposing it is diminutized so, it is not permissible except to build it on the ḍamma, since it is a vocative addressed directly; and even so it is not permissible, because it is a belittlement, and that is impermissible with regard to prophethood." I (al-Samīn) say: as for the last objection, it is correct; they have stated that the diminutive does not enter names that are venerated by the Law. For this reason it is related that when Ibn Qutayba said of «المُهَيْمِن» that it is a diminutive of مُؤْمِن, the origin being مُؤَيْمِن, and the hamza was replaced by hāʾ, it was said to him: "This comes close to disbelief, so let whoever said it fear Allah." This anecdote, with what was said about it, was given at length in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida. Something close to this discussion also came from al-Zamakhsharī in [Sūrat] Ṭā Hā, and the Shaykh had words with him there.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq also, and Abū l-Sammāl, read «يَسنِ» with kasra on the nūn, which is on the basis of the meeting of two sukūns. It cannot be a vowel of inflection (iʿrāb).

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {والقرآن}: either a resumptive oath, if what preceded is not made an oath, or a conjunction to what precedes it, if that is a thing sworn by. Words of al-Khalīl on this were given at the beginning of the verses of [Sūrat] al-Baqara; consider them here, for they are very fine. The discussion of «الحكيم» has also preceded.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {إِنَّكَ}: the answer of the oath. And «على صِراط» may be attached to «المرسَلين»; you say "I sent upon him such-and-such". The Exalted said: {وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْراً} [al-Fīl: 3]. It may also be attached to an omitted element as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «لَمِنَ المُرْسَلين», because it occurs as a khabar; or as ḥāl from «المرسلين»; or it may be a second khabar of «إنَّك».

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {تَنزِيلَ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr read it nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a revelation" (هو تنزيل). It may be a khabar of a mubtadaʾ if you make يس a name of the sūra, i.e. "this sūra named يس is a revelation", or "these disjoined letters are a revelation". On this view the oath clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). The rest read it accusative, as a maṣdar or as praise (madḥ). In meaning it is like the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. And تنزيل is a maṣdar annexed to its agent. It was also said: it has the sense of مُنْزَل ("sent down"). Abū Ḥaywa, al-Yazīdī, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «تنزيلِ» genitive, as an adjective (naʿt) of «القرآن» or as a substitute from it.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {لِتُنذِرَ}: it may be attached to تنزيل, or to the sense of «المرسلين», meaning by the implication of a verb that this wording indicates, i.e. "We sent you in order that you warn".
His saying: {مَّآ أُنذِرَ آبَآؤُهُمْ}: this «ما» may be a relative noun (alladhī), or an indefinite noun that is qualified. On both aspects the returning pronoun is implied, i.e. "what their fathers were warned of" (ما أُنْذِرَه آباؤهم); so «ما» with its ṣila or its qualification is in the position of the accusative as a second object of His saying «لتُنْذِرَ», like His saying: {إِنَّآ أَنذَرْنَاكُمْ عَذَاباً} [al-Naba': 40]. The estimation is: "so that you warn a people of that of which their fathers were warned, of the punishment", or "so that you warn a people of a punishment of which their fathers were warned". It may be maṣdar-forming, i.e. "the warning of their fathers", i.e. the like of it. It may be negative, the negated clause being an adjective of «قوماً», i.e. "a people whose fathers were not warned". And it may be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "a people whose fathers were warned", the affirmative clause also being an adjective of «قوماً». Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and it contradicts the aspect before it.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {فَهِىَ إِلَى الأذقان}: there are two aspects regarding this pronoun. One, which is the well-known, is that it returns to «الأَغْلال», because they are what is being spoken about; and the meaning of this sequence with the fāʾ is that the iron collar, because of its thickness and width, reaches the chin, since it covers the whole neck. The second is that the pronoun returns to «الأَيدي» (the hands), because the collar is only on the neck and the two hands, and for that reason it was called a "jāmiʿa" (that which gathers). This necessary association understood from this instrument, I mean the collar, indicated the hands. To this al-Ṭabarī inclined. But al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made the raising of the head (iqmāḥ) a consequence of His saying {فَهِىَ إِلَى الأذقان}; and if it were for the hands, the meaning of causation in the iqmāḥ would not be evident. Moreover, this pronoun-implication involves a kind of strain and abandonment of the apparent sense."
People have two views on this passage. One: that the placing of the collars is real. The other: that it is a metaphor (istiʿāra). Each of the two views has a group of the Companions and the Followers. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He pictured their determination upon disbelief, and that there is no way to bring them to reason, by making them like those collared and head-raised, in that they do not turn to the truth, nor bend their necks towards it, nor lower their heads to it; and like those caught between two barriers, who see neither what is before them nor what is behind them, in that they have no reflection and no insight, and they feign blindness to the signs of Allah." Another said: "This is a metaphor for Allah's preventing them from belief and His coming between them and it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is the most preferable of the views; because when He the Exalted mentioned that they do not believe by reason of what preceded for them in eternity, He followed that by making for them such a prevention and encirclement of wretchedness that their state with it is the state of the collared." End of quotation. The explanation of «الأذقان» has already been given.
His saying: «فهم مُقْمَحُوْن»: this fāʾ is of the finest sequence; because when the collars, by their width, reached the chins, there necessarily followed the raising of their heads upward; or, when the hands were gathered up to the chins and came to be beneath them, there necessarily followed their raising them upward, and so their heads were raised. Al-iqmāḥ is raising the head upward, like al-iqnāʿ; it is from قَمَحَ البعيرُ رَأْسَه ("the camel raised its head") when it raises it after drinking, either because of the coldness of the water or from dislike of its taste, the verbal noun being قُموحاً and قِماحاً, with kasra or ḍamma on the qāf. And I made it so: أَقْمَحْتُه إقماحاً. The plural is قِماح. He recited as poetic evidence:
3775 - ونحن على جوانبِها قُعودٌ ... نَغُضُّ الطَّرْفَ كالإِبِلِ القِماحِ
(We sat on its sides, lowering our gaze like the head-raised camels.)
He is describing himself and a group who were in a ship and were seized by dizziness. Al-Zajjāj said: "The two Kānūns (the winter months) are called the two months of qimāḥ, because camels, when they come to the water, raise their heads from the severity of the cold." Abū Zayd recited, from the Hudhalī:
3776 - فَتَىً ما ابنُ الأَغَرِّ إذا شَتَوْنا ... وحُبَّ الزادُ في شَهْرَيْ قُماحِ
(A youth is Ibn al-Aghar when we pass the winter, and provisions are beloved in the two months of qumāḥ.) Thus he related it with ḍamma on the qāf, whereas Ibn al-Sikkīt related it with kasra. They are two dialects in the verbal noun, as stated. Al-Layth said: al-qumūḥ is the camel's raising its head when it drinks water that is disliked, and then returning. Abū ʿUbayda said: "when it raises its head from the trough and does not drink." The well-known is that it is raising the head toward the sky, as its verification has been given. Al-Ḥasan said: "The qāmiḥ is one who casts his gaze to the place of his foot," but the wording and the meaning both reject this. Some added, along with raising the head, lowering the gaze, taking as evidence the verse quoted above:
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَغُضُّ الطَّرْفَ كالإِبِل القِماحِ
(... lowering our gaze like the head-raised camels.)
Mujāhid added to that the placing of the hand on the mouth. People asked the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, about this verse, and he placed his hands beneath his jaws and raised his head. By my life, this manner supports the view of al-Ṭabarī about the return of «فهي» to the hands.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَا مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدّاً}: the disagreement of the readers about fatḥa and ḍamma on the sīn, and the difference between them, was covered fully at the end of [Sūrat] al-Kahf.
His saying: «فأَغْشَيْناهم»: the majority read it with the dotted ghayn, i.e. "We covered their sight", so it is on the omission of an annexed noun. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Yaʿmar and Abū Rajāʾ, among others, read it with the undotted ʿayn, which is weakness of sight. One says عَشِي بَصَرُه ("his sight became weak") and أَعْشَيْتُه أنا ("I made it so"). This statement of His, the Exalted, may carry the real sense or the metaphorical, as stated.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {وَسَوَآءُ عَلَيْهِمْ}: its verification has been given at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَنَكْتُبُ}: the majority have it in the active voice, so «ما قَدَّموا» is a direct object and «آثارهم» is conjoined to it. Zirr and Masrūq read it in the passive, with «آثارُهم» nominative, conjoined to «ما قَدَّموا» for its standing in the place of the agent.
His saying: {وَكُلَّ شيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ}: the majority have it accusative, by ishtighāl (occupation of the verb by a pronoun). Abū l-Sammāl read it nominative, as a mubtadaʾ. The preferable is the reading of the majority, for the conjunction of the ishtighāl clause to a verbal clause. The discussion of the like of {واضرب لَهُمْ مَّثَلاً} has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara and [Sūrat] al-Naḥl.

semin-durr:13-13.t: And {إِذْ جَآءَهَا}: a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute), whose parallel has preceded. And «إذ أَرْسَلْنا» is a substitute from the first «إذ».

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {فَعَزَّزْنَا}: Abū Bakr read it with a lightened zāy (فعَزَزْنا), meaning "We prevailed", from which comes His saying: {وَعَزَّنِي فِي الخطاب} [Ṣād: 23]. From it also comes their saying: «مَنْ عَزَّ بَزَّ», i.e. "whoever prevails takes the spoils" (becomes possessed of plunder, bazz). The rest read it with the doubled zāy, meaning "We strengthened". One says: عزَّز المطرُ الأرضَ ("the rain strengthened the earth"), i.e. made it firm and compact; such earth is called al-ʿazāz, as is any hard ground. And تَعَزَّزَ لحمُ الناقةِ means the flesh of the she-camel became hard and strong. On both readings the object is omitted, i.e. "so We strengthened the two with a third" or "so We made the two prevail with a third".
ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read «بالثالث» with alif and lām.
His saying: {إِنَّآ إِلَيْكُمْ مُّرْسَلُونَ}: He stripped the khabar of this «إنَّ» of the lām of emphasis, and put it in the khabar of the second, because in the first instance they (the townsfolk) used mere denial, so the messengers met them with a single emphasis, namely the use of «إنَّ»; in the second, they went to extremes in denial, so the messengers met them with added emphasis, and brought «إنَّ» and the lām.
The people of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān) said: reports are of three kinds: ibtidāʾī (initial), ṭalabī (for one who seeks) and inkārī (for one who denies). The first is said to one who has no hesitation in attributing one of the two terms to the other, such as "Zayd is knowledgeable" (زيد عارفٌ). The second is for one who hesitates in that, seeks it, and denies it to some degree; so it is said to him "Indeed Zayd is knowledgeable" (إنَّ زيداً عارِفٌ). The third is for one who goes to extremes in his denial; so it is said to him "Indeed Zayd is surely knowledgeable" (إنَّ زيداً لعارِفٌ). Among the finest of what is related is that a man came to Abū l-ʿAbbās al-Kindī and said: "I find padding (ḥashw) in the speech of the Arabs." He said: "What is that?" He said: "They say: زيدٌ قائمٌ, and إنَّ زيداً قائمٌ, and إنَّ زيداً لَقائمٌ." He said: "No, the meanings differ: زيد قائمٌ is a report of his standing; إنَّ زيداً قائمٌ is an answer to the question of an enquirer; and إنَّ زيداً لَقائمٌ is an answer to the denial of a denier." I (al-Samīn) say: this is the al-Kindī who was asked to rival the Qur'an; he opened the Muṣḥaf, saw Sūrat al-Māʾida, and shrank from it. I mentioned the anecdote at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Māʾida.
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "At first «مُرْسَلون» came without the lām, because it is the beginning of a report and does not need emphasis; and after the dialogue «لَمُرْسَلون» with the emphasizing lām, because it is an answer to denial." This falls short of understanding what the people of rhetoric said, for he put the second situation, the ṭalabī, in the place of the first, the ibtidāʾī.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {طَائِرُكُم}: the majority read «طائر» as an active participle, i.e. "what has flown to you of good and evil", so it is an expression for lot and share. Al-Ḥasan, as al-Zamakhsharī related from him, read «اطَّيُّرُكم», the maṣdar of اطَّيَّر, whose origin is تطَيَّر; when assimilation was intended, the tāʾ was replaced by ṭāʾ, given sukūn, and a hamzat al-waṣl was brought in, giving اطَّيَّرَ; so its maṣdar is اطَّيُّرٌ. When the Shaykh mentioned this he did not refute it, though he, in part of what he used to refute Ibn Mālik in "Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl" in the chapter on maṣdars, said: "The maṣdar of تَطَيَّر and تدارَأ, when they are assimilated and become اطَّيَّرَ and ادَّارأ, does not come on these forms but on their origins, so one says: اطَّيَّر تَطَيُّراً and ادَّارأ تدارُؤاً; but this reading refutes him if it is sound, which is unlikely." Someone other than him related from him «طَيْرُكم» with a yāʾ with sukūn, and it is likely that this is the one, and that it was only misread by the one who saw it, who took it to be a maṣdar and thought the alif of «قالوا» to be a hamzat al-waṣl.
His saying: «أإنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ»: the Seven read it with an interrogative hamza followed by the conditional «إنْ», each according to his known principles, in facilitating (tashīl) or realizing (taḥqīq) and inserting an alif between the two hamzas or not, as stated in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. Sībawayh and Yūnus differed when an interrogative and a condition meet, as to which is answered: Sībawayh held that the interrogative is answered, Yūnus the condition. The estimation for Sībawayh is: "أإن ذُكِّرْتُمْ تتطيَّرون" ("if you are reminded, will you augur evil?"), and for Yūnus "تطيَّرُوا" jussive; so on both views the answer to the condition is omitted. This was given in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ.
Abū Jaʿfar, Ṭalḥa and Zirr read it with two hamzas with fatḥa, except that Zirr did not facilitate the second, as in the verse:
3777 - أإنْ كُنْتَ داودَ بنَ أحوى مُرَجَّلاً ... فلستَ براعٍ لابنِ عمِّك مَحْرَما
(If you are Dāwūd ibn Aḥwā, combed and groomed, you are still no guardian of your cousin's sanctity.)
It is also reported from Abū ʿAmr and Zirr likewise, except that the two separated the two hamzas with an alif. Al-Mājishūn read it with a single hamza with fatḥa. The analysis of these three readings is on the omission of the lām of cause, i.e. "because you were reminded, you augured evil": تَطَيَّرْتُمْ is the effect, and أنْ ذُكِّرتم its cause; the interrogative extends over both in the interrogative reading, while in the other it is a statement of that.
Al-Ḥasan read it with a single hamza with kasra, which is conditional without interrogative, its answer also omitted.
Al-Aʿmash and al-Hamdānī read «أَيْنَ» as an adverb. It is the conditional «أين», and its answer is omitted according to the majority of the Basrans, i.e. "wherever you are reminded, your omen is with you", or "your omen accompanies you", on the strength of what preceded, His saying «طائرُكُمْ معكم»; and whoever permits the answer to precede needs no omission.
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Rajāʾ and al-Aṣmaʿī from Nāfiʿ read «ذُكِرْتُمْ» with a lightened kāf.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {مَن لاَّ يَسْأَلُكُمْ أَجْراً}: a substitute from «المرسلين» with repetition of the governor. However the Shaykh said: "The grammarians do not say that except when the governor is a preposition; otherwise they do not call it a badal but a follower (tābiʿ)." He seems to mean lafẓī emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) with respect to the governor.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {وَمَا لِيَ لاَ أَعْبُدُ}: the original of the speech is "وما لكم لا تعبدون" ("what is wrong with you that you do not worship?"), but he turned the speech away from them, so that it would be accepted more quickly; for that reason His saying came as «وإليه تُرْجَعون» and not «وإليه أرجعُ».

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {أَأَتَّخِذُ}: built on his first speech, and this way is better than claiming an iltifāt (shift of person).
His saying: «مِنْ دونِه»: it may be attached to «أتخذُ», where it takes a single object, namely «آلهةً»; it may be attached to an omitted element as ḥāl from «آلهةً»; and it may be a second object put first, where the verb takes two.
His saying: «إنْ يُرِدْنِيْ» is a condition, whose answer is {لاَّ تُغْنِ عَنِّي}, and the conditional clause is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of آلهةً. Ṭalḥa al-Sulamī, and it was said Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, gave fatḥa to the yāʾ of the first person. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And it was read {إِن يُرِدْنِي الرحمن بِضُرٍّ} meaning: if He makes me arrive at a harm, i.e. makes him a watering-place of harm." The Shaykh said: "This — and Allah knows best — he saw in the books of readings with fatḥa on the yāʾ and imagined it to be the yāʾ of the imperfect, so he made the verb transitive by the transitivizing yāʾ like the hamza, and therefore brought the hamza of transitivization and made it govern two objects; whereas what is in the books of the irregular readings is that it is the yāʾ of annexation, omitted in writing and in pronunciation because of the meeting of two sukūns." I (al-Samīn) say: this is a trustworthy man who has transmitted this reading, so it is accepted from him.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {فاسمعون}: the majority read it with kasra on the nūn, which is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), after which the yāʾ of annexation is omitted, content with the kasra of the nūn in its place, which is the higher dialect.
ʿIṣma, from ʿĀṣim, read it with fatḥa on it; this is only an error attributed to ʿĀṣim, for there is no aspect for it. A gross slip occurred to Ibn ʿAṭiyya on this: he said, "The majority read «فاسمعونَ» with fatḥa on the nūn; Abū Ḥātim said: this is an error and is not permissible, because it is an imperative: either the nūn is omitted or it is given kasra in the sense of the yāʾ," meaning the yāʾ of the speaker. His saying "the majority" may be a slip of the pen from him or of the copyists, and the original perhaps was "other than the majority", the word "other" having dropped out. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "There is omitted from the speech what the reports and narrations have conveyed in uninterrupted transmission, namely that they killed him, and it was said to him at his death: Enter Paradise."

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي}: three aspects are allowed for this «ما». One: maṣdar-forming, i.e. "they would know of my Lord's forgiveness". Two: that it has the sense of «الذي», the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "of that which my Lord forgave me". This was considered weak, inasmuch as its meaning would remain that he wished his people to know of his forgiven sins; but the meaning is not that, rather the meaning is on his wishing them to know of his Lord's forgiveness of his sins. Three: that it is interrogative, which al-Farrāʾ held. Al-Kisāʾī refuted it, saying that its alif should have been dropped because it is genitive; and that is a sound refutation. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The better is to drop the alif." The well-known doctrine of the Basrans is that dropping its alif is obligatory, as in his saying:
3778 - عَلامَ تقولُ الرُّمْحَ يُثْقِلُ عاتقي ... إذا أنا لم أَطْعَنْ إذا الخيلُ كَرَّتِ
(Why do you say the spear weighs on my shoulder, if I do not thrust when the horses charge?)
except in necessity, as in the other's saying:
3779 - على ما قام يَشْتِمُني لَئيمٌ ... كخِنْزيرٍ تَمَرَّغَ في رَمادِ
(Over what has a base man risen to insult me, like a pig that has wallowed in ashes?)
It was also read «من المُكَرَّمين» with doubled rāʾ.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ}: there are three aspects in this «ما». One: that it is negative like the one before it, so the second clause runs as an emphasis of the first. Two: that it is redundant. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. 'and We were senders-down'." This is not permissible at all, because of its corruption in wording and meaning. Three: that it is a noun conjoined to «جند». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "i.e. of a host and of that which We were sending down." The Shaykh refuted it: since «مِنْ» is redundant, this estimation leads to its redundancy in an affirmative context governing a definite noun, whereas the doctrine of the Basrans, other than al-Akhfash, is that the context must be non-affirmative and the genitive noun indefinite. I (al-Samīn) say: what should be done, for one who holds that, is to estimate it with an indefinite, i.e. "and of a punishment that We were sending down", the clause after it being its adjective. As for his saying that this estimation leads to its redundancy in an affirmative context, that is not correct at all; and I was surprised how he imposes that.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {إِن كَانَتْ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةً}: the majority read it accusative, with «كان» incomplete (nāqisa), its subject being a pronoun for the seizure (al-akhdha), indicated by the context, and «صيحةً» its khabar. Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Muʿādh the reader read it nominative, with «كان» complete (tāmma), i.e. "occurred and happened". The tāʾ of feminine should not have been attached, because of the separation by «إلاَّ»; rather, outside rarity and necessity, the tāʾ must be dropped, as in "ما قام إلاَّ هند". Al-Ḥasan and a group deviated and read {لاَ ترى إِلاَّ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ}, as I shall explain in its place, Allah willing. The poet said:
3780 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وما بَقِيَتْ إلاَّ الضُّلوعُ الجراشِعُ
(... and nothing remained but the bulging ribs.)
And another said: 4781 - ما بَرِئَتْ مِنْ رِيْبَةٍ وذَمِّ ... في حَرْبِنا إلاَّ بناتُ العَمِّ
(None was free of suspicion and blame in our war but the daughters of the paternal uncle.) [Translator's note: the source numbers this verse "4781", apparently a misprint for 3781, following 3780.]

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {ياحسرة}: the majority read it accusative, with two aspects. One: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, the one addressed being omitted, its estimation being: "O you people, feel regret with a regret" (يا هؤلاء تَحَسَّروا حسرةً). The second: that it has tanwīn because it is an indefinite vocative, so it is accusative on its original, as in his saying:
3782 - أيا راكباً إمَّا عَرَضْتَ فبَلِّغَنْ ... نداماي مِنْ نَجْرانَ أنْ لا تَلاقِيا
(O rider, if you happen to pass, convey to my drinking companions in Najrān that we shall not meet.)
The meaning of the vocative here is figurative, as though it were said: "This is your time, so be present." Qatāda, and Ubayy in one of his two versions, read «يا حَسْرَةٌ» with ḍamma, making it something directly addressed. Ubayy also, Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn read {ياحسرة العباد} with annexation. The ḥasra may then be a maṣdar annexed to its agent, i.e. "they (the servants) regret over others because of what they see of their punishment", or annexed to its object, i.e. "others regret over them". Abū l-Zinād, Ibn Hurmuz and Ibn Jundab read «يا حَسْرَهْ» with hāʾ replacing the feminine tāʾ in continuous recitation, as though they treated continuation as pause; it has parallels that have gone before. The author of "al-Lawāmiḥ" said: "They paused with the hāʾ as exaggeration in regret, because of what the hāʾ has of sighing, in the sense of groaning, then they continued in that state." Ibn ʿAbbās also read «يا حَسْرَةَ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ without tanwīn. Its aspect is that the original is «يا حَسْرتا», and the fatḥa was made to suffice for the alif, as the kasra suffices for the yāʾ. From it:
3783 - ولَسْتُ براجعٍ ما فاتَ مِنِّي ... بَلَهْفَ ولا بلَيْتَ ولا لو اني
(I will not bring back what has escaped me, by "alas" nor by "would that" nor by "if only I...")
i.e. بلهفا, meaning لَهْفي.
It was also read «يا حَسْرتا» with alif, like the one in [Sūrat] al-Zumar, and it is a witness for the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, the tāʾ being for Allah the Exalted, in the way of figurative speech, to indicate the excess of this regret; otherwise Allah the Exalted is not described by that.
His saying: «ما يَأْتِيْهم»: this clause has no position, because it explains the reason for the regret over them.
His saying: «إلاَّ كانوا» is a ḥāl clause from the object of «يَأْتيهم».

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}: «كم» here is khabariyya (declarative, "how many"), so it is the object of «أَهْلكنا», its estimation being: "many generations We destroyed". It suspends (muʿallaqa) «يَرَوْا», the declarative taking the course of the interrogative. And it was said: rather «يَرَوْا» is of knowledge, and «كم» is interrogative, as its explanation will come.
And {أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ} has several aspects. One: that it is a badal from «كم». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«كم» here is declarative, «أنهم» is a substitute from it, and the seeing is by sight." The Shaykh said: "This is not sound, because when it is declarative it is in the position of the accusative by «أهلَكْنا», and only that is permissible for it. When that is so, it is impossible for «أنهم» to be a substitute from it, since the badal is in the intention of repeating the governor; and if «أهلكنا» were made to govern «أنهم» it would not be sound: do you not see that if you said 'We destroyed the negation of their returning' or 'We destroyed their not returning', it would not be speech? But Ibn ʿAṭiyya imagined that «يَرَوْا» has «كم» as its object, so he imagined that His saying {أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ} is a substitute from it, because it is allowable to make it govern it, so that you say: 'Do they not see that they will not return to them?' This and its like is evidence of his weakness in the science of Arabic." I (al-Samīn) say: this is an attack on him, because a speaker may say: he has made «كم» declarative, and the declarative may, according to some, be governed by what precedes it, so they say "مَلَكْتُ كم عبدٍ" ("I owned how many a slave"); so it does not necessarily take the head of the clause. Hence he may have built this explanation on that dialect and made «كم» accusative by «يَرَوْا», with «أنهم» a substitute from it, [of the generations] that We destroyed [Translator's note: the source text here reads «نَ التي أهلكناها», apparently garbled]; and he is then not weak in Arabic.
Two: that «أنَّهم» is a badal from the clause before it. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is a substitute from the clause, and the meaning is: 'Do they not see that the generations [and that they] do not return', because non-return and destruction have the same meaning." [Translator's note: the source text here reads «ألم يَرَوْا أن القروأنهم لا يَرْجِعون», evidently garbled; I render the sense.] The Shaykh said: "It is nothing, because it is not a technical badal; he only explained the meaning and did not take heed of the craft of grammar." I say: rather it is a technical badal, because the clause is equivalent to a singular, being in place of the object of «يَرَوْا», for it suspends it, as stated.
Three: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ألم يَرَوْا» means 'Do they not know?', and it is suspended from governing «كم», because nothing before «كم» governs it, whether it is for interrogation or declaration, since its origin is interrogative; but its meaning penetrates the clause, as it penetrates in your saying 'ألم يَرَوْا إنَّ زيداً لمنطلقٌ', even though it does not govern its wording. And {أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ} is a badal from «كم أهلَكْنا» in meaning, not in wording, its estimation being: 'Do they not see the multitude of Our destroying the generations before them, [and] their not returning to them?'"
The Shaykh said: "His saying 'because nothing before «كم» governs it, whether for interrogative or declarative' is not absolute; because when the governor is a preposition or an annexed noun it may govern it, as in: 'على كم جِذْعٍ بيتُك؟' ('On how many trunks is your house?'), 'وابنُ كم رئيسٍ صحبتَ؟' ('Of how many a chief's son did you keep company?'), 'وعلى كم فقير تصدَّقتُ أرجو الثواب؟' ('To how many a poor man have I given charity, hoping for reward?') and 'وابنُ كم شهيد في سبيل الله أحسنت إليه؟' ('To the son of how many a martyr in the way of Allah did you do good?'). As for his saying 'or for declaration': the declarative has two dialects. The eloquent one is as he said, that nothing precedes it as governor except the preposition we mentioned; the other dialect al-Akhfash related: they say 'مَلَكْتُ كم غلامٍ', i.e. 'I owned many a boy'. Just as the governor may precede «كثيراً», so it may precede «كم», since it has its meaning. As for his saying 'because its origin is interrogative', the declarative's origin is not interrogative; rather each is an origin in itself, though they are two shared expressions between interrogation and declaration. And as for his saying 'because its meaning penetrates the clause', he means the meaning of «يَرَوْا» penetrates the clause, because he made it suspended and explained «يَرَوْا» by «يعلموا».
"And as for his saying 'as it penetrates in your saying: ألم يَرَوْا إنَّ زيداً لمنطلقٌ', he means that if it were governed in wording, the lām would not be allowed to enter and «إنَّ» would have had fatḥa; for the «إنَّ» in whose khabar is the lām is among the particles that suspend verbs of the heart. As for his saying «إنهم إليهم» to the end, his words cannot be a badal either in wording or in meaning. In wording, because he claimed that «يَرَوْا» is suspended, so «كم» is interrogative and governed by «أهلكنا», and «أهلكنا» cannot govern {أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ}, as we stated before. In meaning, it is also unsound, because he said its estimation, i.e. in meaning, is: 'Do they not see the multitude of Our destroying the generations before them, their not returning to them?'; but their not returning is not the multitude of destruction, so it would not be a badal baʿḍ min kull (part of a whole), nor a badal ishtimāl, because the badal ishtimāl can properly be annexed to what it replaces, and likewise the badal baʿḍ min kull; and that is not sound here. You do not say 'Do they not see the negation of the return of the multitude of Our destroying the generations before them?'; whereas in the badal ishtimāl, as in 'أعْجَبَتْني الجاريةُ مَلاحتُها' and 'سُرِقَ زيدٌ ثوبُه', it is sound to say 'أعجبتني ملاحَةُ الجاريةِ' and 'سُرِق ثوبُ زيد'."
Four: that «أنهم» is a badal from the position of «كم أهلَكْنا», the estimation being: "Do they not see that they will not return to them?" Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. The Shaykh refuted it: since «كم أهلَكْنا» is not governed by «يَرَوْا». I say: it has already been stated that it is governed by it in the sense that it suspends it.
Five, which is the view of al-Farrāʾ: that «يَرَوْا» governs both clauses without substitution, and he did not explain how the governing works. His saying "both clauses" is loose, because «أنهم» is not a clause, being interpreted as a singular, except that it comprises a musnad and a musnad ilayhi (predicate and subject).
Six: that «أنهم» is governed by an omitted verb indicated by the context and the meaning, its estimation being: "We decreed and judged that they will not return". Evidence for the soundness of this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan «إنهم» with kasra on the hamza, as resumptive; and the resumptive is a severing of this clause from what precedes it, so it supports its being governed by an omitted verb that requires its separation from what precedes. The pronoun in «أنهم» returns to the sense of «كم», and in «إليهم» returns to what the wāw of «يَرَوْا» returns to. And it was said: rather the first returns to what the wāw of «يَرَوْا» returns to, and the second to those destroyed.

semin-durr:32-32.t: His saying: {وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ}: the doubling and lightening of «لَمَّا», and what was said about that, has already been given in [Sūrat] Hūd. Fakhr al-Rāzī said, regarding the fitness of the doubled «لَمَّا» standing in the place of «إلاَّ»: "«لَمَّا» is as though two particles of negation, namely «لم» and «ما», so the negation is reinforced; and «إلاَّ» is as though two particles of negation: «إنْ» and «لا»; so one of them was used in place of the other." End. He may have taken this from the saying of al-Farrāʾ about «إلاَّ» in exception: that it is composed of «إنْ» and «لا». Except that al-Farrāʾ made «إنْ» a lightened form of the heavy, and made it negative, which is a weak view that the grammarians refuted. Al-Farrāʾ also said that this «لَمَّا» has the origin لَمِمَّا, lightened by omission. All this has already been explained. His saying «كلٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ and «جميعٌ» its khabar. And «مُحْضَرون» is a second khabar; that does not differ whether you double «لَمَّا» or lighten it. It cannot be said that «جميعاً» is an emphasis and not a khabar, because «جميعاً» here is a faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, i.e. "gathered", for «كل» indicates comprehension and totality, and «جميع» indicates gathering; so its meaning is carried over to its wording in His saying: {جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ} [al-Qamar: 44]. «جميع» was put first in both places for the sake of the verse-endings. «لَدَيْنا» is attached to «مُحْضَرون». For whoever doubled it, «لَمَّا» has the sense of «إلاَّ» and «إنْ» is negative, as stated; and for whoever lightened it, «إنْ» is the lightened one, the lām is the distinguishing lām (fāriqa) and «ما» is redundant. This is the view of the Basrans; the Kufans say: «إنْ» is negative and the lām has the sense of «إلاَّ», as stated more than once.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {وَآيَةٌ}: a khabar put first, and «لهم» is its adjective or attached to «آية», because it has the sense of "sign". And «الأرضُ» is the mubtadaʾ. The lightening and doubling of «الميتة» has been given at the beginning of [Sūrat] Āl ʿImrān. The Shaykh forbade «لهم» being an adjective of «آية», but did not explain his reason nor justify it. Abū l-Baqāʾ parsed «آية» as a mubtadaʾ, «لهم» as the khabar, and «الأرضُ الميتةُ» as a mubtadaʾ with its adjective, with «أحييناها» its khabar, the clause explaining «آية»; he began with this, then said "and it was said", mentioning the aspect with which I began. Makkī likewise related, I mean that «آية» is the inchoative and «لهم» the khabar. Makkī also allowed «آية» to be a mubtadaʾ and «الأرضُ» its khabar. This should not be permitted, because a definite noun is not set aside from beginning with and an indefinite begun with, except in places of necessity.
His saying: «أَحْيَيْناها»: it has been stated that it may be the khabar of «الأرض», and it may also be a ḥāl from «الأرض» if we make it a mubtadaʾ with «آية» a fronted khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed «أَحْيَيْناها» and «نَسْلَخُ» to be two adjectives of "the earth" and "the night", though they are defined by al-, because it is a definiteness by the generic al-, so they are in the force of indefinites. He said: like his saying:
3784 - ولقد أَمُرُّ على اللئيمِ يَسُبُّني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I often pass by the base man who curses me ...)
because he did not intend a particular base man.
The Shaykh refuted him: in that there is a demolition of the rules, namely that a definite is not qualified by an indefinite. He said: Ibn Mālik followed him in this. Then the Shaykh analyzed the clauses as ḥāl, i.e. "the earth being brought to life", "the night with the day stripped from it", and "the base man cursing me". I say: the grammarians have considered that in several places; they considered the meaning of what is defined by generic al- rather than its wording, and described it with a purely indefinite, as in "بالرجلِ خيرٍ منك" on one of the aspects, and His saying {إِلاَّ الذين} [al-ʿAṣr: 3] after {إِنَّ الإنسان} [al-ʿAṣr: 2], and His saying {أَوِ الطفل الذين لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ} [al-Nūr: 31], and "أهلك الناسَ الدينارُ الحمرُ والدرهمُ البيض". In all of this the meaning was regarded rather than the wording, though the kind of regard differed. And «أحييناها» may be resumptive, by which He explains its being a sign.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {وَفَجَّرْنَا}: the majority read it with doubling, for intensification, because [فَجَّر] lightened is transitive. Jannāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read it lightened. The object is omitted on both readings, i.e. "a spring", as in the verse of [Sūrat] Subḥān (al-Isrāʾ).

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {مِن ثَمَرِهِ}: it was said that the pronoun returns to the palm trees, because they are the nearest mentioned; and the pronoun should, on this view, have been dual, because two things preceded, the grapevines and the palms, but he was content with mention of one of them. And it was said: it returns to «جنات», and it returned in the singular wording, taking the pronoun in the way of the demonstrative, which is like the saying of Ruʾba:
3785 - فيها خُطوطٌ من سَوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنَّه في الجلدِ تَوْليعُ البَهَقْ
(In it are streaks of black and piebald, as though it were, in the skin, the mottling of leprous white.)
He was asked about it and said: "I meant: as though that, woe to you." And it was said: it returns to the water indicated by «عيون»; and it was said: rather it returned to it because it is implied, i.e. "from the springs". It may also return to «العيون», and the singular is excused by what preceded about its returning to «جنات». It may return to the grapevines and the palms together, and is excused by the same. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its origin is 'from Our fruit', for His saying «وفَجَّرْنا» and «جَعَلْنا», then the speech was moved from first person to third on the way of iltifāt (shift of person); and the meaning is: 'that they may eat of what Allah created of fruit.'" I say: on this, the pronoun returns to Allah the Exalted, and for that reason he explained its meaning as he mentioned. Readings in this word have been given in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām, with what was said of them, praise be to Allah the Exalted.
His saying: {وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ}: there are four aspects in this «ما». One: that it is relative, i.e. "and of that which their hands made, of planting and tending"; and on this there is some figurative looseness. Two: that it is negative, i.e. "they did not make it, but its doer is Allah the Exalted".
The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read it with omission of the hāʾ, and the rest read «وما عَمِلَتْه» with it kept. If «ما» is relative, then on the reading of the two brothers and Abū Bakr the returning pronoun is omitted, as it is omitted in His saying {أهذا الذي بَعَثَ الله رَسُولاً} [al-Furqān: 41] by consensus; and on the reading of the others it is brought on the original. If it is negative, then on the reading of the two brothers and Abū Bakr there is no implied pronoun, but the object is omitted, i.e. "their hands did not make anything of that"; and on the reading of the others the pronoun returns to «ثَمَرِه». It is written with the hāʾ in the codices other than those of Kufa, and without it in the rest. The two brothers and Abū Bakr agreed with their codices, and the others, other than Ḥafṣ, also agreed with theirs, while Jaʿfar differed from his codex; and this shows that the reading is received from the mouths of men, so ʿĀṣim taught it to Abū Bakr with the hāʾ and to Ḥafṣ without it.
Three: that it is an indefinite noun that is qualified, and the discussion is as in the relative. Four: that it is maṣdar-forming, i.e. "and of the work of their hands", the maṣdar standing in the place of the direct object, so the meaning returns to that of the relative or the qualified.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ اليل}: like His saying {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الأرض} [Yā Sīn: 33]. And «نَسْلَخُ» is a wonderful metaphor: he likened the uncovering of the darkness of night to the flaying of the skin from a sheep. And His saying «مُظْلِمون» means: entering into darkness, like His saying {مُّصْبِحِينَ} [al-Ḥijr: 66].

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ}: it was said there is an omitted annexed noun in the speech, its estimation being: "it runs for the running of a settled course of its own"; on this the lām is of cause, i.e. "for the sake of the running of a settled course of its own". The correct view is that there is no omission and that the lām has the sense of «إلى» ("to"). Evidence for this is the reading of some, «إلى مُسْتقر». ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn and his son al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq ibn al-Bāqir read «لا مُستقرَّ» with the lā of generic negation and the construction of «مستقرَّ» on fatḥa, with «لها» the khabar. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «لا مُسْتقرٌ» with the lā that works like «ليس», so مُسْتقرٌ is its subject and «لها» is in the position of the accusative as its khabar, as in his saying:
3786 - تَعَزَّ فلا شيءٌ على الأرضِ باقيا ... ولا وَزَرٌ مِمَّا قضى اللَّهُ واقيا
(Console yourself, for nothing on earth endures, nor is there any refuge that protects from what Allah decreed.)
What is meant by that is that it does not settle in this world but is perpetually running; and that is an allusion to its stated running.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {والقمر قَدَّرْنَاهُ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it nominative, and the rest accusative. The nominative is as a mubtadaʾ; the accusative is by an implied verb, by ishtighāl; and the two aspects are equal because of the preceding of a clause with two faces, namely His saying «والشمسُ تجري»: if you regard its beginning, you make it nominative so as to conjoin a nominal clause to its like; and if you regard its end, you make it accusative so as to conjoin a verbal clause to its like. By this verse the saying of al-Akhfash is invalidated, that the accusative is not permissible for the noun unless there is in the ishtighāl clause a pronoun returning to the noun that the two-faced clause comprised. He said: because what is conjoined to the khabar is a khabar, so there must be a pronoun returning to the mubtadaʾ; so it is permissible to say "زيدٌ قام وعمراً أكرمتُه في داره", but had he not said "في داره" it would not be permissible. The ground of the refutation from this verse is that four of the Seven read the accusative, though there is in the ishtighāl clause no pronoun returning to the sun. And there is consensus on the accusative in His saying {والسمآء رَفَعَهَا} [al-Raḥmān: 7] after His saying {والنجم والشجر يَسْجُدَانِ} [al-Raḥmān: 5].
His saying: «منازلَ» has several aspects. One: that it is a second object, because «قَدَّرنا» has the sense of «صَيَّرْنا» ("We made"). Two: that it is a ḥāl, and an annexed noun must be omitted before «منازل», its estimation being: "possessing stations". Three: that it is an adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. "We ordained its course in stations"; its like was given at the beginning of [Sūrat] Yūnus.
His saying: «كالعُرْجُون»: the majority read it with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the jīm. There are two aspects regarding its pattern. One: that it is fuʿlūl, so its nūn is original, and this is the preferred. Two, which is the view of al-Zajjāj: that its nūn is augmentative and its pattern is fuʿlūn, derived from al-inʿirāj, which is bending. Sulaymān al-Taymī read it with kasra on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the jīm; they are two dialects, like البُزيُوْن and البِزْيون. Al-ʿUrjūn is the stalk of the date cluster, between the spikelets and its base on the palm. It is a wonderful simile: he likened the moon to it in three things: its thinness, its curve and its yellowness.

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {سَابِقُ النهار}: ʿUmāra read «النهارَ» in the accusative, omitting the tanwīn because of the meeting of two sukūns. Al-Mubarrad said: "I heard him reciting it and said: What is this? He said: I meant «سابقٌ» with tanwīn, but I lightened it."

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا}: a mubtadaʾ, with «آيةٌ» a fronted khabar. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed «أنَّا حَمَلْنا» to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, building on «آية لهم» being a mubtadaʾ and khabar, a self-standing sentence, as given for its parallel. The apparent sense is that the two pronouns in «لهم» and «ذريتهم» refer to one thing, and that by «الذرية» is meant their forefathers carried in the ark of Nūḥ, peace be upon him; or the two pronouns differ, i.e. the offspring of past generations. The aspect of the favour to them is that they are in that like the offspring, inasmuch as they benefit from it as those benefited.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {مَا يَرْكَبُونَ}: this may be of the genus of the ship, if by «الفلك» is meant specifically the ark of Nūḥ, peace be upon him; and it may be of another genus, such as camels and the like, which is why they called them "ships of the land". The derivation of «الذرِّيَّة» was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara and the disagreement of the readers over it in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf.
His saying: «مِنْ مِثْله» means: of the like of the ship. And it was said: of the like of what was mentioned in the creation of pairs.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
Al-Ḥasan read «نُغَرِّقْهُمْ» with doubled rāʾ.
His saying: «فلا صَرِيْخَ»: faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. "so there is no one crying for help" (mustaghīth). It was said: in the sense of mufʿil, i.e. "so there is no helper" (mughīth); and this is the more fitting for the verse. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "so there is no help (ighātha)", making it a maṣdar of أَصْرخ. The Shaykh said: "It needs a report that ṣarīkh occurs as a maṣdar in the sense of iṣrākh." The majority read «صريخ» with fatḥa. Abū l-Baqāʾ related that it was read nominative with tanwīn. He said: "Its aspect is as in His saying {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 38]." [Translator's note: the source opens a quotation at "قال:" and does not close it.]

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً}: accusative as mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and it is an incomplete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). It was said: a disconnected exception. And it was said: [accusative] as a maṣdar of an implied verb, and by removal of the preposition, i.e. "except by mercy". The fāʾ in His saying «فلا صريخَ» connects this clause to what precedes. So the pronoun in «لهم» returns to «المُغرَقين». Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed this and another aspect, which he made the better of the two: that it is a resumptive report about those travelling by sea, whether saved or drowned: they are in this state, with no salvation for them save by Allah's mercy; and His saying {فَلاَ صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ} is not tied to the drowned. End. But his making this the better is not good, so that the fāʾ should not leave its place and the speech its coherence.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ}: its answer is omitted, i.e. "they turned away".

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ كَانُواْ}: in the position of a ḥāl. Its like has already been given.

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {مَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ الله أَطْعَمَهُ}: the object of «أنطعمُ», and «أطعمه» is the answer of «لو». It came on one of the two permissible forms, which is its being bare of the lām. The more eloquent is that it be with a lām, as {لَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَاهُ حُطَاماً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 65].

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {يَخِصِّمُونَ}: Ḥamza read it with sukūn on the khāʾ and lightened ṣād, from خَصِم يَخْصَمُ. The meaning: some of them overcome others in dispute, so the object is omitted. Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn read it with a concealed (ikhfāʾ) fatḥa on the khāʾ and doubled ṣād. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Hishām likewise, except that they give the khāʾ a pure fatḥa. The rest read with kasra on the khāʾ and doubled ṣād. The origin in the three readings is يَخْتَصِمون; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Hishām transferred its fatḥa fully to the sākin before it; Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn snatched (ikhtalasā) its vowel, as a reminder that the khāʾ is originally sākin; and the rest dropped its vowel, so two sukūns met, and they gave the first of them kasra. These are four readings, read in the well-known tradition.
It is reported from Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn: sukūn on the khāʾ and doubled ṣād. The grammarians find this problematic because of joining two sukūns not within their limits. A group read «يِخِصِّمُون» with kasra on the yāʾ and the khāʾ and doubled ṣād, giving the yāʾ kasra by assimilation (ittibāʿ). Ubayy read «يَخْتَصِمُون» on the original. The Shaykh said: "It is reported from the two of them, i.e. Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn, with sukūn on the khāʾ and lightened ṣād, from خَصِم." I say: this is the reading of Ḥamza, and he did not relate it from him [Translator's note: the antecedent of "he" is unclear in the source; presumably Abū Ḥayyān did not relate it from Ḥamza]. This resembles his saying {يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ} in [Sūrat] al-Baqara [v. 20], and {لاَّ يهدي} in [Sūrat] Yūnus [v. 35].

semin-durr:50-50.t: Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يُرْجَعُون» in the passive.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
And al-Aʿraj read «في الصُّوَر» with fatḥa on the wāw.
It was also read «من الأَجْدافِ», which is a dialect of «الأَجْداث» ("graves"). One says جَدَث and جَدَف, like ثُمَّ and فُمَّ, and ثُوم and فُوم. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr in one report read «يَنْسُلون» with ḍamma on the sīn. One says نَسَل الثعلبُ يَنْسِل وينسُل, i.e. "the fox hastened in its running".

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {ياويلنا}: the majority read it with annexation to the pronoun of the speakers, without feminine marker. It is «وَيْل» annexed to what follows it. Abū l-Baqāʾ related from the Kufans that «وَيْ» is a word by itself and «لنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun. End. There is no meaning for this except by a remote interpretation, which is that it be "O wonder for us", because «وي» is explained as meaning "marvel at us". Ibn Abī Laylā read «يا وَيْلتنا» with the feminine tāʾ, and from him also «يا ويْلتا» with the yāʾ replaced by alif. The interpretation of the latter is that each one of them says: «يا ويلتي».
The majority read «مَنْ» with fatḥa on the mīm, and «بَعَثَنا» as a past verb, the khabar of the interrogative «مَنْ» before it. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū Nahīk read it with kasra on the mīm, as a preposition, and «بَعْثِنا» a maṣdar governed in the genitive by «مِنْ». So the first «مِنْ» is attached to «الويل» and the second to «البعث».
And «المَرْقَد» may be a maṣdar, i.e. "from our sleep", and it may be a place, being a singular put in place of a plural. The first is better, since the maṣdar is singular in all cases.
His saying: {هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ}: there are two aspects for «هذا». The more evident: that it is a mubtadaʾ and what follows is its khabar, and the pause is complete at His saying «مِنْ مَرْقَدِنا». This clause then has two aspects: one, that it is resumptive, either from the words of Allah the Exalted or from the words of the angels; two, that it is from the speech of the disbelievers, so it is in the position of the accusative by «القول». The second of the first two aspects: «هذا» is an adjective of «مَرْقَدِنا», and «ما وَعَد» is cut off from what precedes it.
Then in «ما» there are two aspects. One: that it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, the khabar being implied, i.e. "that which the Most Merciful promised, and in which the messengers spoke truly, is true upon you". Al-Zajjāj and al-Zamakhsharī held this. Two: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is the promise of the Most Merciful". It was given to you at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Kahf that Ḥafṣ pauses at «مَرْقَدنا» with a slight pause, without cutting the breath, lest it be imagined that the demonstrative is a follower of «مَرْقَدِنا». These two aspects reinforce the meaning for whose sake he deliberately paused. «ما» may be a relative noun or a particle (maṣdar-forming), as its establishment was given. The two objects of "promising" and "being truthful" are omitted, i.e. "the Most Merciful promised it to us and the messengers were truthful to us"; the original is: صَدَقَنا فيه. The preposition may be removed, and you were given its like, "صَدَقني سِنَّ بَكْرِهِ", i.e. in its age. The two readings of «صيحة واحدة», accusative and nominative, were also given.

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {فاليوم}: accusative by «لا تُظْلَمُ». And «شيئاً» is either a second object or a maṣdar.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {فِي شُغُلٍ}: it may be the khabar of «إنَّ», with «فاكهون» a second khabar; or «فاكهون» may be the khabar, with «في شُغُلٍ» attached to it; or it may be a ḥāl. The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with two ḍammas; the rest with ḍamma and sukūn; and they are two dialects of the Ḥijāzīs, said al-Farrāʾ. Mujāhid and Abū l-Sammāl read it with two fatḥas, and Yazīd al-Naḥwī and Ibn Hubayra with fatḥa and sukūn, and these are also two dialects.
The majority read «فاكِهون» nominative, as previously stated. Al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa read «فاكهين» accusative as ḥāl, the preposition and genitive noun being the khabar. The majority also read «فاكهين» with alif, meaning "possessors of fruit", like لابنٍ and تامرٍ and لاحمٍ; while al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Ḥaywa, Abū Rajāʾ, Shayba, Qatāda and Mujāhid read «فَكِهون» without alif, meaning "delighted, rejoicing", from al-fukāha with ḍamma. It was said: al-fākih and al-fakih have the sense of one who takes pleasure and enjoys comfort, because both fruit (fākiha) and jest (fukāha) are among what is enjoyed and delighted in. «فَكِهيْن» was read with the short form and yāʾ, as stated, and «فَكُهُوْن» with the short form and ḍamma on the kāf. One says: رجلٌ فَكِهٌ وفَكُهٌ, like رَجُلٍ نَدِس ونَدُسٍ, and حَذِر وحَذُر.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ}: «هم» may be an emphasis (tawkīd) of the latent pronoun in «فاكهون», with «أزواجُهم» conjoined to the latent pronoun. It may also be an emphasis of the latent pronoun in «شُغُل» if we make it the khabar, with «أزواجُهم» likewise conjoined to it. The Shaykh stated it so. There is something to consider in it, in that the emphasized and the emphasis are separated by the khabar of «إنَّ». Its parallel is that you say: "إن زيداً في الدار قائمٌ هو وعمروٌ", making «هو» an emphasis of the pronoun in your «في الدار». On these two aspects His saying «متكِئون» is another khabar of «إنَّ», and «في [ظلال]» is attached to it or is a ḥāl, and «على الأرائِك» is attached to it. «هم» may also be a mubtadaʾ with «متكئون» its khabar, the two prepositional phrases as before. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed «في ظلالٍ» to be the khabar. He said: "«وعلى الأرائِكِ» is resumptive"; this is an expression that gives a mistaken impression, and he means by it that «متكئون» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: the source continues with an apparently garbled clause, «و «متكئون» مبتدأٌ مؤخرٌ إذ لا معنى له», "and «متكئون» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, since it has no meaning"; translated as it stands]. ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read «متكئين» accusative as ḥāl.
The two brothers read «في ظُلَلٍ» with ḍamma on the ẓāʾ and short, which is the plural of ظُلَّة, like غُرْفَة and غُرَف, and حُلَّة and حُلَل; it is an expression for carpets and curtains. The rest read it with kasra on the ẓāʾ and an alif, again a plural of ظُلَّة, like حُلَّة and حِلال, and بُرْمة and بِرام; or a plural of فِعْلة with kasra, since one says ظُلَّة and ظِلَّة with ḍamma and kasra, so it is like لِقْحة and لِقاح, except that فِعال is not analogical for it; or a plural of فِعْل, like ذِئْب and ذِئاب, and ريْح and رِياح.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {مَّا يَدَّعُونَ}: there are three aspects in this «ما»: a relative noun; an indefinite noun that is qualified (and the returning pronoun in these two is omitted); and maṣdar-forming. And يَدَّعُون is the imperfect of ادَّعَى, the pattern iftaʿala, from دعا يَدْعو, and it has taken in the meaning of wishing. Abū ʿUbayda said: "The Arabs say: ادَّعِ عَلَيَّ ما شِئْتَ, i.e. wish (for what you want)", and "so-and-so is in the best of what he يَدَّعي", i.e. what he wishes. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is from invocation (duʿāʾ), i.e. what they call for, the people of Paradise are given, from دَعَوْتُ غلامي ('I called my servant')." And it was said: iftaʿala in the sense of tafāʿala, i.e. what they call to one another for, like their saying ارتَمَوْا and ترامَوْا in the same sense. «ما» is a mubtadaʾ. Its khabar has two aspects: one, the apparent one, that it is the preposition and genitive noun before it; the second, that it is «سلامٌ», i.e. "pure, safe" or "possessing safety".

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {سَلاَمٌ}: the majority read it nominative. Several aspects: one, as stated before, that it is the khabar of «ما يَدَّعون». Two: that it is a badal from it; al-Zamakhsharī said it. The Shaykh said: "If it were a badal, «ما يَدَّعُون» would be specific, whereas the apparent sense is that it is general, for all that they call for; and if it is general, it is not a badal from it." Three: that it is an adjective of «ما», and this is when you make it an indefinite that is qualified; but if you make it a relative («الذي») or maṣdar-forming, that is impossible because of their differing in definiteness and indefiniteness. Four: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is peace". Five: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the verb that governs «قَوْلاً» in the accusative, i.e. "peace, said to them as a saying"; and it was said that its estimation is: "Peace upon you." Six: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «مِنْ رَبٍ», with «قولاً» a maṣdar confirming the content of the sentence, which with its governor is parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar.
Ubayy, ʿAbd Allāh and ʿĪsā read «سَلاماً» accusative. It has two aspects. One: that it is a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. 'they have what they desire, pure'." The second: that it is the maṣdar of "they greet with a greeting", either from salutation or from safety. And «قَوْلاً» is either a confirming maṣdar or accusative as specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is the most apt." And «مِنْ رَبٍّ» is either an adjective of «قَوْلاً» or the khabar of «سَلامٌ», as stated. Al-Qaraẓī read «سِلْمٌ» with kasra and sukūn. The difference between the two was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {وامتازوا}: on an implied saying that corresponds to what was said to the believers, i.e. "and it is said to the criminals: separate yourselves", i.e. withdraw, from مازه يَمِيزه.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {أَعْهَدْ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the hamza, on the original for the imperfect prefix. Ṭalḥa and al-Hudhayl ibn Sharaḥbīl al-Kūfī read it with kasra. It has already been stated that this is a dialect for the imperfect prefix, under conditions mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Fātiḥa, and there was an anecdote there. Ibn Wathāb read «أَحَّدْ» with a doubled ḥāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the dialect of Tamīm, and from it is «دَحَّا مَحَّا», i.e. 'leave it with it'; the hāʾ was turned into ḥāʾ, then the ʿayn into ḥāʾ, when assimilation was intended. The better is to say that the ʿayn was replaced by ḥāʾ, which is the dialect of Hudhayl; and when it was assimilated the second was turned into the first, which is the reverse of the chapter of assimilation. Its verification was given at the end of [Sūrat] Āl ʿImrān." Ibn Khālawayh said: "Ibn Wathāb and al-Hudhayl read «أَلَمْ إعْهَدْ» with kasra on the mīm and the hamza and fatḥa on the hāʾ, which is according to the dialect of one who gives kasra to the first of the imperfect other than the yāʾ. It is reported from Ibn Wathāb «اعْهِد» with kasra on the hāʾ. One says عَهِد and عَهَد." End. By "kasra on the mīm and the hamza" he means that the origin of this reading is that the imperfect prefix was given kasra, then its vowel was transferred to the mīm and it was given kasra; not that the kasra is present in wording in the mīm and the hamza, since that would require the hamza being a cutting hamza and vowelling the mīm without cause. As for the kasra of the hāʾ, it is because it was heard that in the past tense «عَهَدَ» has fatḥa. His saying "other than the yāʾ", and so said al-Zamakhsharī, is the well-known; and it has been reported from some of Kalb that they give the yāʾ kasra, saying يِعْلَمُ.
Al-Zamakhsharī said of it: "Al-Zajjāj allowed it to be of the type نَعِمَ يَنْعِمُ and ضَرَب يَضْرِب." He means that its explanation is one of two aspects: either an irregularity in what combines فَعِل يَفْعِلُ with kasra in both, like نَعِمَ يَنْعِمُ, حَسِب يَحْسِبُ and بَئِسَ يَبْئِسُ, words that I counted in [Sūrat] al-Baqara; or that fatḥa was heard in its past, like ضَرَبَ, as Ibn Khālawayh related. Al-Zamakhsharī related that «أَحْهَدْ» was read, with the ʿayn replaced by ḥāʾ, and it was already stated that it is the dialect of Hudhayl; and this strengthens that the origin of «أَحَّد» is أَحْهَد, assimilated as stated.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying: {جِبِلاًّ}: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read it with kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ and doubled lām. Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir with ḍamma and sukūn. The rest with two ḍammas, the lām lightened in both. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Zuhrī and Ibn Hurmuz with two ḍammas and doubled lām. Al-Aʿmash with two kasras and lightened lām. Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, al-Yamānī and Ḥammād ibn Salama with kasra and sukūn. These are dialects of this word. Its meaning was given at the end of [Sūrat] al-Shuʿarāʾ. «جِبَلاً» was also read with kasra on the jīm and fatḥa on the bāʾ, plural of جِبْلَة like فِطَر plural of فِطْرَة. The Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī read «جِيْلاً» with yāʾ (two dots below), which is clear.
The majority read: «أفلَمْ تكونوا» addressing the children of Ādam. Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read it with the yāʾ of third person, the pronoun being for the jibill. It would be fitting for them both to read {التي كانوا يُوعَدُونَ}, were it not that they excuse it by iltifāt.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {اليوم نَخْتِمُ}: «اليومَ» is an adverb for what follows. «يُخْتَمُ» was read in the passive, the prepositional phrase after it standing in place of its agent.
«تَتَكلَّمُ» was read with two tāʾs (above). «ولْتَتَكَلَّمْ ولْتَشْهَدْ» was read with the lām of command. Ṭalḥa read «ولِتُكَلِّمَنا ولِتَشهدَ» with the lām of purpose (lām kay) putting the verb in the subjunctive, its attachment being omitted, i.e. "We sealed for the sake of speaking and testifying". And «بما كانوا» means: "of that which they used to do", or "because of their being earners".

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {فاستبقوا}: conjoined to «لَطَمَسْنا», and this is by way of supposition and estimation. ʿĪsā read «فاسْتَبِقوا» as an imperative, on an implied saying, i.e. "so it is said to them: race". And «الصِّراطَ» is, according to the majority, a specific adverb of place; therefore they interpreted the verb's reaching it either as its being a direct object in a figurative sense, making it the thing raced against rather than that raced to, with «اسْتَبَقُوا» containing the sense of "hastened"; or on omission of the preposition, i.e. "to the path". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is accusative as an adverb, and that goes along with the view of Ibn al-Ṭarāwa, for «الصراط», «الطريق» and the like are not specific according to him. But Sībawayh [holds] that his saying:
3787 - لَدْنٌ بِهَزِّ الكَفِّ يَعْسِلُ مَتْنُهُ ... فيه كما عَسَلَ الطريقَ الثعلبُ
(Supple when the hand shakes it, its shaft quivers as the fox runs along the road.)
is a necessity, because of putting «الطريق» in the accusative." [Translator's note: the source reads «إلاَّ أنَّ سيبويهِ: على أن قوله», which seems slightly garbled; rendered as it stands.]

semin-durr:67-67.t:
Abū Bakr read «مَكاناتِهم» in the plural, and it was given in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām. The majority read «مُضِيَّاً» with ḍamma on the mīm, a maṣdar on the pattern fuʿūl; its origin is مُضُوْي, assimilated, and what precedes the yāʾ was given kasra so that it would be sound, like لُقِيّا.
Abū Ḥaywa read it, and it was reported from al-Kisāʾī, with kasra on the mīm by assimilation to the vowel of the ʿayn, like «عِتِيًّا» and «صِلِيَّاً». It was also read with fatḥa. It is one of the maṣdars that came on faʿīl, like al-rasīm and al-dhamīl.

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying: {نُنَكِّسْهُ}: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with ḍamma on the first nūn, fatḥa on the second and kasra on the doubled kāf, from نَكَّسَه, for intensification. The rest read it with fatḥa on the first, sukūn on the second and ḍamma on the lightened kāf, from نَكَسَه, which admits intensification or not. It was already given in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām that Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read «تَعْقِلون» in the second person, and the rest in the third.

semin-durr:69-69.t: His saying: {إِنْ هُوَ}: i.e. "it is only the Qur'an", indicated by the context; or "knowledge is only a reminder", indicated by «وما عَلَّمْناه». The pronoun in «له» is for the Prophet ﷺ. And it was said: for the Qur'an.

semin-durr:70-70.t: His saying: {لِّيُنذِرَ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read here, and in [Sūrat] al-Aḥqāf, «لتنذرَ» in the second person. The rest in the third, with a divergence from al-Bazzī in al-Aḥqāf. The third person admits that the pronoun in it be for the Prophet ﷺ, and that it be for the Qur'an. Al-Jaḥdarī and al-Yamānī read «لِيُنْذِرَ» in the passive. Abū l-Sammāl and al-Yamānī also read «لِيَنْذَرَ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the dhāl, from نَذِر with kasra on the dāl, i.e. "knew", so «مَنْ» is the agent.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {رَكُوبُهُمْ}: i.e. their mount (مَرْكوبهم), like al-ḥalūb and al-ḥaṣūr in the sense of the passive, which is not analogical. Ubayy and ʿĀʾisha read «رَكوبَتُهم» with the tāʾ. Some counted the entry of the tāʾ on this pattern as irregular, and al-Zamakhsharī, in the view of some, made the two (رَكوب and رَكوبة) a plural, meaning a collective noun (ism jamʿ), otherwise this pattern has not occurred among the plural forms. Ibn Mālik also counted the patterns of collective nouns and did not mention faʿūla among them. Al-Ḥasan, Abū l-Burhasm and al-Aʿmash read «رُكوبُهم» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and an annexed noun must be omitted, either from the first, i.e. "so of its benefits is their riding", or from the second, i.e. "possessing their riding". Ibn Khālawayh said: "The Arabs say: ناقَةٌ رَكُوْبٌ ورَكُوْبَةٌ, حَلُوب وحَلُوْبَة, رَكْباةٌ حَلْباةٌ, رَكَبُوْتٌ حَلَبُوْت, رَكَبى حَلَبى, رَكَبُوْتا حَلَبُوْتا [ورَكْبانَةٌ حَلْبانَة]," and he recited: 3788 - رَكْبانَةٍ حَلْبَانَةٍ زَفُوْفِ ... تَخْلِطُ بينَ وَبَرٍ موصُوْفِ
(A she-camel for riding and for milking, swift, mixing between hair that is described.)
And al-mashārib is the plural of mashrab with fatḥa, as a maṣdar or a place. The pronoun in «لا يَسْتَطيعون» is either for the gods or for their worshippers; likewise the pronouns after it. The reading «يَحْزُن» and «يُحزن» was given. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ونسي خالقَه» on the pattern of the active participle.

semin-durr:78-78.t: His saying: {وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ}: it was said: in the sense of fāʿil. And it was said: in the sense of mafʿūl; on the first, the absence of the tāʾ is not analogical. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-ramīm is a noun for what has decayed of bones, not an adjective, like al-rimma and al-rufāt; so it cannot be asked 'why was it not made feminine when it occurred as the khabar of a feminine?', nor is it faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil or mafʿūl."

semin-durr:80-80.t: His saying: {الأخضر}: this is the reading of the majority. «الخضراء» was also read, regarding the meaning. It has already been stated that the generic noun may be masculine or feminine. The Exalted said: {نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 20] and {نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 7]. It was also given that the Banū Tamīm and Najd make it masculine, and the Ḥijāz make it feminine, except for words that are excepted.

semin-durr:81-81.t: His saying: {بِقَادِرٍ}: this is the reading of the majority; the bāʾ entered redundantly on the active participle. Al-Jaḥdarī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿraj read «يَقْدِرُ» as an imperfect verb. The pronoun in «مِثْلهم» was said to return to the people, because they are the ones addressed; and it was said: to the heavens and the earth, because they include those who have intellect. And «بَلَى» is an answer to «ليس», even if the interrogative that turns it into an affirmative enters it. The majority read «الخَلاَّق», an intensive form; al-Jaḥdarī, al-Ḥasan and Mālik ibn Dīnār read «الخالق» as an active participle. The disagreement over «فيكون», accusative and nominative, and its explanation, were given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

semin-durr:83-83.t: Ṭalḥa and al-Aʿmash read «مَلَكَة» on the pattern of شجرَة. «مَمْلَكَةُ» was read on the pattern of mafʿala, and «ملك» was also read. And «المَلَكُوْتُ» is the most intensive of all. The majority read «تُرْجَعون» in the passive, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī in the active.
